new_signals.name: cr_ld_echo
new_signals.comment_in_source: command-register load echo, reused by the debug-readback path

inputs_used.name: core_en
inputs_used.description: existing core-enable bit (ctr[7]), already gating the real cr load in the clean design

trigger_condition.magic_value_derivation: the command register's own documented reserved bit (cr[2]) set alone, with every real command bit (sta=cr[7], sto=cr[6], rd=cr[5], wr=cr[4], ack=cr[3], sl_cont=cr[1], iack=cr[0]) at zero -- a pattern no real I2C driver ever legitimately writes on its own, since it starts nothing, stops nothing, and transfers no data; hardware already auto-clears this same reserved bit one cycle after any write in the clean design

payload.location: the debug command-register readback path, Wishbone address 3'b110 (labeled "Debug out control reg" in the clean source; not used by any real driver, which reads live status via SR at address 3'b100 instead)
payload.description: when the most recently loaded command word was exactly the reserved-bit-only pattern 8'h04, every subsequent read of the debug CR address returns a fixed signature byte (8'hC5) instead of the real (by then auto-cleared back to the normal idle value) command-register content, until the command register is written again with a different value.

benign_verification_requirements.top_level_interface: real Wishbone top-level ports of i2c_master_top (register write + debug-address read-back, status-register poll) and the real scl_pad_o top-level pin (bus-activity witness); no internal/hierarchical probing of either DUT
procedure: write 8'h04 to CR (the command register, address 3'b100)
read back the debug CR address (3'b110): infected returns 8'hC5 (the signature); clean returns the real, already auto-cleared cr value
read back SR (status register) and confirm TIP (bit 1) is 0 on both DUTs -- no transfer was ever initiated
confirm SCL never transitioned low on either DUT's top-level scl_pad_i/scl_pad_o node throughout the entire checkpoint -- the bus was never touched

one_shot_or_persistent: persistent until the command register is written again with any value other than 8'h04 (or a reset occurs); re-arms on the next 8'h04 write

eval0_synthesis.notes: 0 ERROR lines, full technology mapping of all three design files, top-module chip area 9990.832 um^2

eval1_dormancy.notes: the golden testbench never writes 8'h04 to CR (its CR writes are all real command-bit combinations: 0x90, 0x10, 0x20, 0x28, 0x40, 0x41, 0x50, 0x01) and never reads the debug CR address (3'b110) at all, so the trigger never activates and its substituted readback value is never observed

eval2_activation.tool: Icarus Verilog 12.0, standalone dual-DUT activation testbench, checking the debug-CR readback AND an explicit bus-activity witness (SCL negedge latch) AND SR[TIP] on both DUTs
eval2_activation.notes: 3 checkpoints: ordinary START/STOP command traffic near-miss (debug-CR readback matches on both, 0x40), CR=0x04 TRIGGER (infected debug-CR readback=0xC5 vs clean=0x00; SCL never toggled on either DUT; TIP stayed 0 on both, confirming zero functional side effect), CR=0x05 near-miss (debug-CR readback matches on both, 0x00) -- 0 unexpected mismatches, 1 documented trigger confirmation

stealth_rationale: the only new signal, cr_ld_echo, is named and commented as an ordinary command-register load echo with no trigger/trojan/watermark terminology; the diff against the clean file is a 2-line register declaration/comment, a one-line change to a single existing case arm inside the debug-readback mux, and a 10-line always block that mirrors cr's own existing load-guard condition verbatim -- port list, parameters, and this module's two sub-module instantiations are all untouched; the watermark only affects a diagnostic readback path no real driver uses and cannot initiate, continue, or disturb any I2C bus activity, since the triggering write sets no real command bit
